title: DEP: Database-Enforced Privacy. A Design Proposal
description: A design for a database server in which privacy is part of the type system, the query semantics, and the execution engine. Protected values can be used for matching one value at a time but are never returned by ordinary queries; linking whole datasets and disclosing values are allowed only in functions declared LINKS and DISCLOSES, so every such place is reviewable and listed in the catalog. Includes a privacy-first development method in which the privacy policy, the schema, and the tests are the same artifact.
